_readme: Template for tools/mcp-healer/mcp_healer.py. Copy it to a file you own, fill every {{PLACEHOLDER}}, and set each server's action: ensure (install), park (keep but do not load), remove, or ignore (leave untouched). Optional servers ship as ignore (off). Keys are ${ENV} references or a headersHelper command: put the values in your environment (or OS credential store), never in this file; the healer refuses an entry whose placeholder or ${VAR} is still unset. 'egress' says where your data goes; check it against your organisation's policy before enabling a server. Versions verified when this release was built; re-pin deliberately.

tokensave.egress: none: local code index (.tokensave/ in each repo)
tokensave.reason: Local code graph: callers, impact, dead code, without reading whole files. Pinned, checksum-verified binary; see mcp/README.md.

playwright.egress: local browser; reaches only the sites you point it at
playwright.reason: OPTIONAL, off by default: the Playwright CLI (package playwright-cli, guide 45) is the preferred browser path. Browser automation for testing your own web apps. Exact version pinned (never @latest); isolated profile, so it never uses your signed-in browser.

chrome-devtools.egress: local browser; upstream defaults send usage statistics and performance-trace URLs (CrUX lookups) to the vendor: both switched off here
chrome-devtools.reason: OPTIONAL: performance traces, network and console inspection of your own pages. Keep --no-usage-statistics and --no-performance-crux.

context7.egress: HOSTED: every query goes to a third-party service
context7.reason: OPTIONAL: current library documentation. Works without a key at lower limits. Never put code, internal names or secrets in a query.

github.egress: HOSTED: GitHub's MCP endpoint, read-only tools; repository data your account can already read flows into the session
github.reason: OPTIONAL. Default for github.com, SAML and Enterprise Managed Users orgs: the token comes from your gh login through headersHelper, so there is no new secret in any file. Needs the GitHub CLI OAuth app approved for your org. The /readonly URL limits the tools, not the token, which stays as broad as your gh login: use github-pat for a narrow token. An organisation IP allow list blocks this hosted endpoint (HTTP 403): use github-local. Dynamic toolsets no longer exist upstream; X-MCP-Toolsets picks what is exposed.

github-pat.egress: HOSTED: GitHub's MCP endpoint, read-only tools; repository data the token can read flows into the session
github-pat.reason: OPTIONAL, least privilege: a fine-grained token limited to the repositories you name, read access to contents, issues, pull requests and actions. The variable has its own name on purpose: Claude Code reads some well-known credential names as empty in remote headers. An organisation may need an owner to approve the token, and Enterprise Managed Users orgs must allow personal tokens. Keep the value in your environment or credential store.

github-ghe.egress: HOSTED: your GHE.com tenant's MCP endpoint, read-only; repository data the token can read flows into the session
github-ghe.reason: OPTIONAL, GHE.com data-residency tenants (replace {{GHE_SUBDOMAIN}} with your tenant name; the healer refuses the entry until you do). Read-only comes from the header because a /readonly path is not documented for this host. The enterprise must allow personal tokens. GitHub Enterprise Server has no remote endpoint: use github-local or the gh CLI.

github-local.egress: LOCAL process; calls the GitHub API from your own network with your gh token; read-only, lockdown on
github-local.reason: OPTIONAL fallback when an organisation IP allow list blocks the hosted endpoint. Run gh_mcp_local.py github.com --install once (pinned release, SHA-256 checked). Replace github.com with your tenant host for GHE.com. GitHub Enterprise Server is EXPERIMENTAL: GitHub documents the local server there, Anthropic's GHES page says use the gh CLI, so prove it on your instance first.

find.egress: none: local index on this machine
find.reason: Registered by setup: the find skill's search, show and related as MCP tools for subagents and the desktop app. Local index, no network. The skill and CLI stay the primary interface.

mslearn.egress: HOSTED: queries go to Microsoft; public documentation only, no sign-in
mslearn.reason: OPTIONAL: search and fetch Microsoft Learn documentation. Needs no account. Never put internal names or code in a query.

azure.egress: LOCAL process; calls Azure Resource Manager with your own az login and RBAC rights; results enter the session
azure.reason: OPTIONAL Azure MCP server (MIT), read-only, stable 2.0 line pinned. Acts with whatever your az login can already reach; it adds no access. Run az login first.

azure-devops.egress: LOCAL process; calls Azure DevOps for the organisation you name, with your az login; results enter the session
azure-devops.reason: OPTIONAL Azure DevOps MCP server (MIT), local mode on your Azure CLI login. Replace {{ADO_ORG}} with your organisation name. The hosted remote endpoint needs your own Entra app registration for Claude Code, so it is not listed.

atlassian.egress: HOSTED: Atlassian's Rovo MCP endpoint; Jira and Confluence content your account can read flows into the session; some calls use Rovo credits
atlassian.reason: OPTIONAL, Jira and Confluence Cloud only (Data Center is not supported by this endpoint). Sign in with /mcp (OAuth). An Atlassian admin can block the endpoint ('Allow Atlassian supported domains'). Write tools exist: review what you approve.

bigquery.egress: HOSTED: Google Cloud's BigQuery MCP endpoint; query text and results for projects you can access, audit-logged by Google
bigquery.reason: OPTIONAL. Needs a Google Cloud project with the BigQuery API enabled and the roles MCP Tool User, BigQuery Job User and BigQuery Data Viewer for your identity, plus your own OAuth client (desktop type); enter its secret when Claude Code asks, never in this file. Prefer a separate read-only identity.

gcloud.egress: HOSTED: Google Cloud CLI remote MCP endpoint (public preview); runs gcloud and bq commands as you, audit-logged by Google
gcloud.reason: OPTIONAL, PREVIEW. Needs the cloudcli API enabled and the MCP Tool User role in the project, plus your own OAuth client (desktop type). It can run mutating commands with your rights: leave it off unless you need it.

ms365.reason: OPTIONAL community server (MIT, not bundled): read-only mail, calendar and meeting transcripts through YOUR OWN tenant app registration (public client, delegated permissions Mail.Read, Calendars.Read, OnlineMeetings.Read, OnlineMeetingTranscript.Read.All). Needs tenant-admin consent for those permissions, and the tenant must allow transcripts (the Graph transcript calls return 403 when policy turns them off). Set WB_MS365_CLIENT_ID and WB_MS365_TENANT_ID first: the healer refuses this entry until both are set, and the vendor's built-in multi-tenant app is never used. Have your security team review the package at this pinned version before you enable it. Sign in once with the package's --login in a folder you own.

brave-search.egress: HOSTED: queries go to Brave Search API
brave-search.reason: OPTIONAL web search. Needs a key. Claude Code's built-in WebSearch covers most needs.

exa.reason: OPTIONAL neural web search. Needs a key (or sign in by OAuth via /mcp and drop the header).

tavily.reason: OPTIONAL search and extract. Needs a key.

postgres.egress: LOCAL process; connects only to the database in DATABASE_URI; query results flow into the session
postgres.reason: OPTIONAL read-only Postgres (crystaldba/postgres-mcp, MIT): schema, EXPLAIN, index advice. Restricted mode = read-only transactions. Point it at a dev or replica database you are allowed to query, with a read-only role; never production data your role should not see.
